zion: 1. (Jewish Antiq.) A hill in Jerusalem, which, after the capture of that city by the Israelites, became the royal residence of David and his successors. 2. Hence, the theocracy, or church of God. 3. The heavenly Jerusalem; heaven.
zincographic: Of or pertaining to zincography; as, zincographic processes.
zincite: Native zinc oxide; a brittle, translucent mineral, of an orange-red color; -- called also red zinc ore, and red oxide of zinc.
zirconlight: A light, similar to the calcium light, produced by incandescent zirconia.
zinnia: Any plant of the composite genus Zinnia, Mexican herbs with opposite leaves and large gay-colored blossoms. Zinnia elegans is the commonest species in cultivation.
zillah: A district or local division, as of a province. [India]
zizith: The tassels of twisted cords or threads on the corners of the upper garment worn by strict Jews. The Hebrew for this word is translated in both the Authorized and Revised Versions (Deut. xxii. 12) by the word "fringes."
zirconium: A rare element of the carbon-silicon group, intermediate between the metals and nonmetals, obtained from the mineral zircon as a dark sooty powder, or as a gray metallic crystalline substance. Symbol Zr. Atomic weight, 90.4.
zincking: The act or process of applying zinc; galvanization.
zinc: An abundant element of the magnesium-cadmium group, extracted principally from the minerals zinc blende, smithsonite, calamine, and franklinite, as an easily fusible bluish white metal, which is… | To coat with zinc; to galvanize.
zimb: A large, venomous, two-winged fly, native of Abyssinia. It is allied to the tsetse fly, and, like the latter, is destructive to cattle.
zimocca: A sponge (Euspongia zimocca) of flat form and fine quality, from the Adriatic, about the Greek islands, and the coast of Barbary.
zinnwaldite: A kind of mica containing lithium, often associated with tin ore.
zigzag: 1. Something that has short turns or angles. The fanatics going straight forward and openly, the politicians by the surer mode of zigzag. Burke. 2. (Arch.) A molding running in a zigzag line; | Having short, sharp turns; running this way and that in an onward course.
zirconic: Pertaining to, containing, or resembling, zirconium; as, zirconic oxide; zirconic compounds. Zirconic acid, an acid of zirconium analogous to carbonic and silicic acids, known only in its salts.
zincoid: Pertaining to, or resembling, zinc; -- said of the electricity of the zincous plate in connection with a copper plate in a voltaic circle; also, designating the positive pole. (old)
zincous: 1. (Chem.) (a) Of, pertaining to, or containing, zinc; zincic; as, zincous salts. (b) Hence, formerly, basic, basylous, as opposed to chlorous. 2. (Physics) Of or pertaining to the positive pole of a galvanic battery; electro-positive.
zincky: , Pertaining to zinc, or having its appearance. [Written also zinky.]
zip: A hissing or sibilant sound such as that made by a flying bullet. | To make, or move with, such a sound.
zingiberaceous: Of or pertaining to ginger, or to a tribe (Zingibereæ) of endogenous plants of the order Scitamineæ. See Scitamineous.
zingel: A small, edible, freshwater European perch (Aspro zingel), having a round, elongated body and prominent snout.
zircon: A mineral occurring in tetragonal crystals, usually of a brown or gray color. It consists of silica and zirconia. A red variety, used as a gem, is called hyacinth. Colorless, pale-yellow or smoky- brown varieties from Ceylon are called jargon. Zircon syenite, a coarse-grained syenite containing zircon crystals and often also elæolite. It is largely developed in Southern Norway.
zincic: Pertaining to, containing, or resembling, zinc; zincous.
zincographical: Of or pertaining to zincography; as, zincographic processes.
zinkenite: A steel-gray metallic mineral, a sulphide of antimony and lead.
zibeth: A carnivorous mammal (Viverra zibetha) closely allied to the civet, from which it differs in having the spots on the body less distinct, the throat whiter, and the black rings on the tail more numerous. Note: It inhabits India, Southern China, and the East Indies. It yields a perfume similar to that of the civet.
zirconoid: A double eight-sided pyramid, a form common with tetragonal crystals; -- so called because this form often occurs in crystals of zircon.
zircofluoride: A double fluoride of zirconium and hydrogen, or some other positive element or radical; as, zircofluoride of sodium.
ziega: Curd produced from milk by adding acetic acid, after rennet has ceased to cause coagulation. Brande & C.
zilla: A low, thorny, suffrutescent, crucifeous plant (Zilla myagroides) found in the deserts of Egypt. Its leaves are boiled in water, and eaten, by the Arabs.
zizania: A genus of grasses including Indian rice. See Indian rice, under Rice.
zincification: The act or process of applying zinc; the condition of being zincified, or covered with zinc; galvanization.
zigzaggery: The quality or state of being zigzag; crookedness. The . . . zigzaggery of my father's approaches. Sterne.
zirconia: The oxide of zirconium, obtained as a white powder, and possessing both acid and basic properties. On account of its infusibility, and brilliant luminosity when incandescent, it is used as an ingredient of sticks for the Drummomd light.
zietrisikite: A mineral wax, vert similar to ozocerite. It is found at Zietrisika, Moldavia, whence its name.
zincing: The act or process of applying zinc; galvanization.
zinco: A combining form from zinc; in chemistry, designating zinc as an element of certain double compounds. Also used adjectively.
zincography: The art or process of engraving or etching on zinc, in which the design is left in relief in the style of a wood cut, the rest of the ground being eaten away by acid.
zincopolar: Electrically polarized like the surface of the zinc presented to the acid in a battery, which has zincous affinity. (old)
zincode: The positive electrode of an electrolytic cell; anode. Miller.
zibet: A carnivorous mammal (Viverra zibetha) closely allied to the civet, from which it differs in having the spots on the body less distinct, the throat whiter, and the black rings on the tail more numerous. Note: It inhabits India, Southern China, and the East Indies. It yields a perfume similar to that of the civet.
zirco: A combining form (also used adjectively) designating zirconium as an element of certain double compounds; zircono-; as in zircofluoric acid, sodium zircofluoride.
zither: An instrument of music used in Austria and Germany. It has from thirty to forty wires strung across a shallow sounding-board, which lies horizontally on a table before the performer, who uses both hands in playing on it. Note: [Not to be confounded with the old lute-shaped cittern, or cithern.]
zikkurat: A temple tower of the Babylonians or Assyrians, consisting of a lofty pyramidal structure, built in successive stages, with outside staircases, and a shrine at the top.
zimentwater: A kind of water found in copper mines; water impregnated with copper.
zincify: To coat or impregnate with zinc.
zif: The second month of the Jewish ecclesiastical year, corresponding to our May.
zionism: Among the Jews, a theory, plan, or movement for colonizing their own race in Palestine, the land of Zion, or, if that is impracticable, elsewhere, either for religious or nationalizing purposes; -- called also Zion movement. --Zi"on*ist, n. -- Zi`on*is"tic (#), a.
zincograph: A zinc plate prepared for printing by zincography; also, a print from such a plate.
